# Rheon model portfolio

## Pressure benchmarks now cover 150 fits

The unified “150 pressure fits · complete GPU requests · 128 consumed cases” view joins the 127
named fits with 23 original-training-output fits. All 185 measured default fit identities now have
GPU accuracy and timing: 150 pressure proposals and 35 full-state generators. Twenty other
components still need appropriately scoped benchmarks. This does not complete all 524 parameter
states or intended solver variants.

For the 23 newly measured pressure fits, median case latency ranges from 2.08794 to 8.65121 GPU ms
per pressure request and worst mean-free pressure error ranges from 0.00602154 to 1.58280. These are
retained experiments, not promoted application-quality models. A pressure request does not advance a
full simulation step; compare it separately from the complete F64 generator results below.

Select both unified pressure partitions to compare all 150 subjects; filter cells per metre
separately from grid X/Y/Z and input dt. Primary timing excludes forward-validation hooks; separate
paired overhead for the additional 23 fits is retained without subtraction. The native maximum chart
shows the maximum over selected case statistics; cards also report the median across case medians.
Original process captures remain at their exact bound paths, and historical measurement tables stay
unchanged.

This project retains 205 recorded fits/components and 524 parameter byte states. All 205 have source
reviews; 35 full-state generator fits now have matched GPU benchmarks. The four F64 baseline
executions are not four new fits. The 127 named pressure fits have a separate 128-request GPU
comparison.

## Matched full-state results

On the same 64 retained native cases, the original F64 cell composition has better worst pressure
error and 7.645–31.085 times lower matched median GPU time than every one of the 35 other generator
fits. This compares distinct retained designs; the best checkpoint has not disappeared or
deteriorated.

| Physical outputs per pass | Worst pressure relative L2 | GPU ms/output, median case | GPU ms/output, 32 cubed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.55386e-16 | 0.25839 | 0.58552 |
| 2 | 2.79755e-16 | 0.17926 | 0.47411 |
| 3 | 2.79755e-16 | 0.14110 | 0.43128 |
| 4 | 2.79755e-16 | 0.12893 | 0.40099 |

Every output includes pressure, all three staggered velocities and tracer, and advances a full 1/60
second. The F64 implementation executes sequential N1 advances; packing K outputs amortizes
transfers and graph-call overhead, rather than learning a shortcut across intermediate states. The
N8-only coordinate change is unused in this regime.

The best pressure tails among the 35 other fits are about 5.24e-4. A controlled K1 diagnostic
locates the fixed-viscosity series' shared 32-cubed worst pressure case mainly in its CNN pressure
fallback. Other pressure-map and request errors remain. The diagnostic does not replace a causal
generator with future reference input.

## Reading the measurements

Choose the retained source titled “Matched GPU generators and F64 baseline”, then select K, grid
dimensions and cells per metre. Plot IDs use model names; b1-v1 and b1-v2 are distinct fits.
Original fit identities and exact process captures remain inspectable. Times cover native CPU input,
packing, known controls, GPU prediction and all owned CPU outputs with synchronization.

The table above reports medians of per-case medians. A native maximum plot reports the maximum of
the selected per-case statistic. Thus “Median GPU time per physical output” on that plot means the
largest case median, not a median across cases. Each fit card includes density/domain tables and the
exact retained source identity.

The population is 16 consumed fitting scenes at four starts, densities 8 and 16 cells/m, and grids
15×6×8, 9×11×11, 16 cubed and 32 cubed. It is not independent holdout evidence or a 600-step
own-history rollout. Resource observations found no competing CUDA compute PID; external host work
was present and continuous hardware exclusivity is not established.

## Historical timing correction

The four earlier “Complete GPU generators” tables retain ten fits measured with a forward-validation
hook inside the timing interval. Their scalar values and original packets stay unchanged. The new
matched tables exclude that hook and preserve all prior output hashes. Paired calibration measures
median hook overhead of 0.0593–0.4997 ms per block across fits. That instrumentation mismatch does
not explain the numerical error gap.

Historical instrumented packet identities:
```text
f6969ec40ad9153a88a474ea7eb4e77d3652b441a7c535763de4253328817f70
ee6a1e516cf9efd181c9f5427037dece7e7c46ec5fe1064ccafaefa9ed325f10
1bd75131441638b77c5509232b2b8afb9f27a068c618a8dd6bb2fc19715a13b9
19954f1816a8748269628cd0728d52c7a53bc61c3c67bc65015ad2da6e827470
```

The quoted near-exact cell and temporal anchors also reproduce on their original populations. Those
use different rectangles, densities or cadences. The original temporal entry requires fine-clock
force schedules absent from these legacy scenes; its cadence results stay separate. No fine
histories were invented for this comparison.

## Model history and remaining work

Pressure-only error/time and complete simulation-output error/time are separate tasks. Guide
summaries explain each method, fitting exposure, purpose and outcome. Authored comparisons organize
evidence; all 94 genuine Trials retain their original unknown ancestry.

Clean GPU training/publication reproduction, remaining component/checkpoint benchmarks and long
drift still need qualification. Thirty-five parameter states remain outside native declarations, and
936 registrations still need disposition. No unique weights are approved for deletion by these
results alone.

Old-Rheon references remain the benchmark authority. The updated Rheon changes fluid behavior and
needs a separate physics epoch with training/test regeneration scripts. Final portable save/load
acceptance and practical fast Open remain unfinished.

# Rheon model portfolio · evidence migration

205 training-receipt card drafts, 379 dashboard aliases and 524 checkpoint byte identities are separately indexed. These are not interchangeable model counts. 55 fit drafts lack a structured method description; original receipts still retain mode/training facts. 51 exact training configurations are now recovered and embedded alongside their original receipts. Architecture source review remains pending. No automatic causal lessons or clean reproduction are claimed.

Pressure results: all 129 named entries are accounted for. 127 have the same 128 original consumed pressure requests each; C01/C02 retain explicit unavailable checkpoint observations. Nine bounded scalar packets retain all 65,024 measured values and 17,536 unavailable observations. Missing timings are not zero. Density and XYZ domain counts remain distinct. Execution variants and device/precision facts are retained per subject. These pressure proposals do not advance a complete simulation.

Both previously quoted full-state anchors reproduced exactly under their actual work contracts. Their historical timings and single-case pressure values cannot be substituted for these common-pressure populations. Full-state/own-history drift and new timings remain separate work.

Open notes/portfolio-index.json for card/alias/checkpoint links. Each card embeds exact original receipt bytes and source-linked facts. Captured historical paths and Run IDs grant no current filesystem/execution authority. No unique model weights are copied into these notes or retired. New Rheon has not been adopted; its different physics requires a separate reference epoch.

## Source-reviewed methods and distinct comparison scopes

Seventeen of 205 fit cards have retrospective source reviews prepared: the shared
spectral pressure response, the local transport sampler, the fixed-viscosity
parent, C106/C107, the three C125/C126/C127 head calibrations and the three C128/C129/C130 pressure-tail calibrations. Original receipts and
configurations remain exact below each authored explanation. Clean retraining
and full portfolio acceptance remain pending.

The spectral pressure response has four learned float64 coefficients fitted on
148 training scenes. The prescribed local sampler has 48 learned float64
parameters fitted on 16 scenes. The fixed-viscosity parent records 100,456 total
parameters and 6,600 trainable parameters, with a frozen 243-coefficient viscosity
kernel. A later composition can replace components and cannot inherit the
parent’s entire active parameter count or training coverage.

C106/C107 each have 93,758 parameters and two internal pressure correction
passes; they do not generate two physical simulation steps. They are matched
siblings starting from the same student initialization. The teacher-loss arm
records 4,800 teacher forwards; the control records zero. The captured optimizer
uses a 10/3 head learning-rate multiplier despite inherited metadata saying

and full portfolio acceptance remain pending.

held-out or freshly qualified speed claim.

are distinct metrics. The N8-labelled cell-coordinate anchor actually takes its

prediction with cheap intermediate frames. All model and source identities,

## What the reduced-integration residual fits actually changed

Four additional cards distinguish S1/S2 AdamW from S3 physical-objective LBFGS
and S4 direct-correction supervision. All use the same10,876-parameter width8
subnet. Of148 counted training scenes,29 provide correction gradients;119
contribute fixed bypass controls. The selected S2 state equals initialization.
S4's improved direct correction loss accompanies a worse physical objective.

The N8 runner replaces eight fine advances with groups2/2/3/1 and three learned
corrections per physical output. K outputs still advance sequentially; this is
not endpoint prediction with cheap intermediate frames. Exact replay preserves
the recorded failures, so those failures cannot be dismissed as a changed
restoration path. These are source reviews, not clean retraining or new timing.


## What the three/four-stage temporal readouts learned

The two macrostep readout fits learn only 9 or 12 global float64 coefficients,
not a new full-state network. They combine the current state and intermediate
states of a frozen three/four-internal-stage backbone into the next 1/60 s output.
The three coefficient groups are pressure, shared velocity and tracer.

Training uses all 148 scenes at two starts, but only 29 N8 scenes produce gradients;
119 N1 scenes contribute fixed losses. All 98 retained N8 evaluation rows fail the
diagnostic 1e-5 gate in each model, while all 920 unchanged N1 rows pass. The four-stage
arm has lower worst pressure/equation errors than three stages on those rows,
but neither establishes accurate reduced integration. K physical outputs still
advance sequentially; internal stages and physical future frames are different.
These are original retained GPU results, not new replay, latency or promotion.


C75/C76/C77 are matched C37 four-correction fits with no/attached/detached auxiliary gradients. Each optimizer sees eight single-mode synthetic patterns, not the retained physical trajectory population; equal updates also have different forward counts.

## Source-reviewed methods and distinct comparison scopes

Seventeen of 205 fit cards have retrospective source reviews prepared: the shared
spectral pressure response, the local transport sampler, the fixed-viscosity
parent, C106/C107, the three C125/C126/C127 head calibrations and the three C128/C129/C130 pressure-tail calibrations. Original receipts and
configurations remain exact below each authored explanation. Clean retraining
and full portfolio acceptance remain pending.

The spectral pressure response has four learned float64 coefficients fitted on
148 training scenes. The prescribed local sampler has 48 learned float64
parameters fitted on 16 scenes. The fixed-viscosity parent records 100,456 total
parameters and 6,600 trainable parameters, with a frozen 243-coefficient viscosity
kernel. A later composition can replace components and cannot inherit the
parent’s entire active parameter count or training coverage.

C106/C107 each have 93,758 parameters and two internal pressure correction
passes; they do not generate two physical simulation steps. They are matched
siblings starting from the same student initialization. The teacher-loss arm
records 4,800 teacher forwards; the control records zero. The captured optimizer
uses a 10/3 head learning-rate multiplier despite inherited metadata saying
1000. The common 128-request diagnostic favors C107’s tails, with no independent
held-out or freshly qualified speed claim.

Pressure relative L2, full-state RMS errors, equation residual and fitting losses
are distinct metrics. The N8-labelled cell-coordinate anchor actually takes its
N1 branch on the quoted case. Existing K-output generators still advance each
physical output in sequence; the reviewed components do not establish endpoint
prediction with cheap intermediate frames. All model and source identities,
parameter populations, integration work and reference epochs remain separate.


The C128/C129/C130 pressure tails each retain 94,956 frozen parent
parameters and fit 33,982 new tail parameters on 1,526 training geometries,
with 202 teacher-development geometries. The actual head-only recipe supersedes
inherited scene-training context for this fit. The tail is bypassed above 16
cells on any axis. Its small-grid pressure scores therefore remain a distinct
scope from complete generators, larger domains and rollout drift.

C125/C126/C127 calibrate the existing1,198-parameter C107 coarse head, with 92,560 frozen fine parameters, using6,004 training and724 development teacher geometries. All three start from the exact same C107 weights. Their teacher covers axes through128, but the retained common pressure evidence covers small grids only. This is separate from the later conditional511-mode tails.

Six C119–C124 follow-ups now distinguish coarse-head learning-rate changes, hard-case resampling, deeper channel redistribution and a larger-head one-pass pressure predictor. The first four share the exact C107 initialization; the two architecture variants bind separate transformed initializations. All record2,400 fine-network forwards, with different sampling/architecture costs. The paired improvements are small and metric-dependent; both architecture variants worsen the common small-grid pressure tails. No new speed or complete-generator qualification follows from this source review.

## What the reduced-integration residual fits actually changed

Four additional cards distinguish S1/S2 AdamW from S3 physical-objective LBFGS
and S4 direct-correction supervision. All use the same10,876-parameter width8
subnet. Of148 counted training scenes,29 provide correction gradients;119
contribute fixed bypass controls. The selected S2 state equals initialization.
S4's improved direct correction loss accompanies a worse physical objective.

The N8 runner replaces eight fine advances with groups2/2/3/1 and three learned
corrections per physical output. K outputs still advance sequentially; this is
not endpoint prediction with cheap intermediate frames. Exact replay preserves
the recorded failures, so those failures cannot be dismissed as a changed
restoration path. These are source reviews, not clean retraining or new timing.


## What the three/four-stage temporal readouts learned

The two macrostep readout fits learn only 9 or 12 global float64 coefficients,
not a new full-state network. They combine the current state and intermediate
states of a frozen three/four-internal-stage backbone into the next 1/60 s output.
The three coefficient groups are pressure, shared velocity and tracer.

Training uses all 148 scenes at two starts, but only 29 N8 scenes produce gradients;
119 N1 scenes contribute fixed losses. All 98 retained N8 evaluation rows fail the
diagnostic 1e-5 gate in each model, while all 920 unchanged N1 rows pass. The four-stage
arm has lower worst pressure/equation errors than three stages on those rows,
but neither establishes accurate reduced integration. K physical outputs still
advance sequentially; internal stages and physical future frames are different.
These are original retained GPU results, not new replay, latency or promotion.


C75/C76/C77 are matched C37 four-correction fits with no/attached/detached auxiliary gradients. Each optimizer sees eight single-mode synthetic patterns, not the retained physical trajectory population; equal updates also have different forward counts.

## Source-reviewed methods and distinct comparison scopes

Seventeen of 205 fit cards have retrospective source reviews prepared: the shared
spectral pressure response, the local transport sampler, the fixed-viscosity
parent, C106/C107, the three C125/C126/C127 head calibrations and the three C128/C129/C130 pressure-tail calibrations. Original receipts and
configurations remain exact below each authored explanation. Clean retraining
and full portfolio acceptance remain pending.

The spectral pressure response has four learned float64 coefficients fitted on
148 training scenes. The prescribed local sampler has 48 learned float64
parameters fitted on 16 scenes. The fixed-viscosity parent records 100,456 total
parameters and 6,600 trainable parameters, with a frozen 243-coefficient viscosity
kernel. A later composition can replace components and cannot inherit the
parent’s entire active parameter count or training coverage.

C106/C107 each have 93,758 parameters and two internal pressure correction
passes; they do not generate two physical simulation steps. They are matched
siblings starting from the same student initialization. The teacher-loss arm
records 4,800 teacher forwards; the control records zero. The captured optimizer
uses a 10/3 head learning-rate multiplier despite inherited metadata saying
1000. The common 128-request diagnostic favors C107’s tails, with no independent
held-out or freshly qualified speed claim.

Pressure relative L2, full-state RMS errors, equation residual and fitting losses
are distinct metrics. The N8-labelled cell-coordinate anchor actually takes its
N1 branch on the quoted case. Existing K-output generators still advance each
physical output in sequence; the reviewed components do not establish endpoint
prediction with cheap intermediate frames. All model and source identities,
parameter populations, integration work and reference epochs remain separate.


The C128/C129/C130 pressure tails each retain 94,956 frozen parent
parameters and fit 33,982 new tail parameters on 1,526 training geometries,
with 202 teacher-development geometries. The actual head-only recipe supersedes
inherited scene-training context for this fit. The tail is bypassed above 16
cells on any axis. Its small-grid pressure scores therefore remain a distinct
scope from complete generators, larger domains and rollout drift.

C125/C126/C127 calibrate the existing1,198-parameter C107 coarse head, with 92,560 frozen fine parameters, using6,004 training and724 development teacher geometries. All three start from the exact same C107 weights. Their teacher covers axes through128, but the retained common pressure evidence covers small grids only. This is separate from the later conditional511-mode tails.

Six C119–C124 follow-ups now distinguish coarse-head learning-rate changes, hard-case resampling, deeper channel redistribution and a larger-head one-pass pressure predictor. The first four share the exact C107 initialization; the two architecture variants bind separate transformed initializations. All record2,400 fine-network forwards, with different sampling/architecture costs. The paired improvements are small and metric-dependent; both architecture variants worsen the common small-grid pressure tails. No new speed or complete-generator qualification follows from this source review.

## Source-reviewed methods and distinct comparison scopes

Seventeen of 205 fit cards have retrospective source reviews prepared: the shared
spectral pressure response, the local transport sampler, the fixed-viscosity
parent, C106/C107, the three C125/C126/C127 head calibrations and the three C128/C129/C130 pressure-tail calibrations. Original receipts and
configurations remain exact below each authored explanation. Clean retraining
and full portfolio acceptance remain pending.

The spectral pressure response has four learned float64 coefficients fitted on
148 training scenes. The prescribed local sampler has 48 learned float64
parameters fitted on 16 scenes. The fixed-viscosity parent records 100,456 total
parameters and 6,600 trainable parameters, with a frozen 243-coefficient viscosity
kernel. A later composition can replace components and cannot inherit the
parent’s entire active parameter count or training coverage.

C106/C107 each have 93,758 parameters and two internal pressure correction
passes; they do not generate two physical simulation steps. They are matched
siblings starting from the same student initialization. The teacher-loss arm
records 4,800 teacher forwards; the control records zero. The captured optimizer
uses a 10/3 head learning-rate multiplier despite inherited metadata saying
1000. The common 128-request diagnostic favors C107’s tails, with no independent
held-out or freshly qualified speed claim.

Pressure relative L2, full-state RMS errors, equation residual and fitting losses
are distinct metrics. The N8-labelled cell-coordinate anchor actually takes its
N1 branch on the quoted case. Existing K-output generators still advance each
physical output in sequence; the reviewed components do not establish endpoint
prediction with cheap intermediate frames. All model and source identities,
parameter populations, integration work and reference epochs remain separate.


The C128/C129/C130 pressure tails each retain 94,956 frozen parent
parameters and fit 33,982 new tail parameters on 1,526 training geometries,
with 202 teacher-development geometries. The actual head-only recipe supersedes
inherited scene-training context for this fit. The tail is bypassed above 16
cells on any axis. Its small-grid pressure scores therefore remain a distinct
scope from complete generators, larger domains and rollout drift.

C125/C126/C127 calibrate the existing1,198-parameter C107 coarse head, with 92,560 frozen fine parameters, using6,004 training and724 development teacher geometries.
